description: GLM consolidated training data — all calibration in one file

patterns.name: AND encoding captures shared structure
patterns.description: The AND of two element vectors captures shared electron density. Combined with bond order, it predicts bond energy with high fidelity.

patterns.name: Pre-snap metrics carry more signal
patterns.evidence: Raw NRCI correlates with chemistry better than snapped NRCI
patterns.description: The raw vector before Golay snap contains more physical information than the snapped vector. The snap cost itself is signal.

patterns.name: Noble gases are the vacuum state
patterns.evidence: HW=0, NRCI=1.0 for He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe
patterns.description: Noble gas Data Objects encode as the zero vector — perfect coherence, no perturbation. They are the substrate's vacuum.

patterns.name: Same-element pairs are invisible
patterns.evidence: AND/XOR gives HW=0 for C-C, N-N, O-O
patterns.description: When both elements are identical, their AND and XOR produce zero vectors. The substrate cannot distinguish C-C from C≡C.

patterns.name: Bond order partially inferable from geometry
patterns.description: The HW of the AND encoding correlates moderately with bond order. The substrate can partially infer single/double/triple from geometry.

patterns.name: Compactness measures geometric regularity
patterns.description: The compactness metric (4π·Area/Perimeter²) approaches 1.0 as shapes become more circular. The substrate naturally measures regularity.

patterns.name: NRCI decreases with pure-element chain length
patterns.evidence: H-F NRCI=0.93, C-C NRCI=0.66, N-N NRCI=0.65
patterns.description: Heteronuclear bonds have higher NRCI than homonuclear chains. The substrate sees electron asymmetry as coherence.

patterns.name: Golay corrects exactly 3 errors
patterns.description: The Golay [24,12,8] code corrects exactly 3 errors as predicted by theory. No more, no less.

patterns.name: Small integers snap to zero
patterns.description: Small integers encoded as 24-bit vectors are 'close to zero' in the Golay metric. The substrate treats them as near-vacuum states.

patterns.name: Golden ratio appears in decagon radius
patterns.description: The regular decagon radius R(10) = 1/(2·sin(π/10)) = φ (golden ratio). Mathematical constants emerge from the substrate's geometry.
